claims.text: High-entropy alloys can comprise five or more principal elements in equal or near-equal atomic ratios.
Multiple principal elements affect configurational entropy, free energy, phase selection, and stability in HEAs.
High configurational entropy can reduce the free energy of simple solid-solution phases, especially at high temperatures.
The high-entropy effect makes chemically ordered intermetallic compounds less competitive with simple solid solutions.
HEA nanoparticles maintain a single-phase solid solution over 473–1923 K when high mixing entropy is complemented by significant lattice distortion.
Significant lattice distortion suppresses atomic diffusion.
A larger spread in constituent atomic radii produces higher lattice distortion.
A higher degree of lattice distortion increases energy barriers for atomic diffusion.
High-temperature solid-solution stability depends on the kinetic barrier to atomic rearrangement.
Reduced atomic diffusion preserves chemical homogeneity and a single phase against temperature-induced segregation or ordering.
HEA nanoparticles with smaller atomic-size mismatches and lower lattice distortion are more prone to diffusion-driven phase separation under otherwise equivalent conditions.
The high-lattice-distortion group will show minimal phase and composition changes relative to its as-synthesized state after high-temperature operation.
The low-lattice-distortion control group will show measurable phase segregation or chemical ordering after high-temperature operation.
The comparison can modify only atomic-size mismatch while holding synthesis method, particle size, initial phase, and other major variables constant.

contradictions.description: The design says atomic-size mismatch is the only major modified variable, but it proposes changing the identities of the constituent metals to alter atomic radii. This necessarily changes elemental chemistry and potentially bonding, mixing enthalpy, oxidation behavior, crystal preference, and diffusivity in addition to size mismatch, so the stated control cannot isolate lattice distortion as written.
